business_patterns.top_pattern: NV Intermountain heart-assist outlier drove TANF Standard hospital cost
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: NV Medicaid TANF Standard acute hospital and IP Med/Surg
key_driver_codes: Aortic and Heart Assist Procedures Except Pulsation Balloon with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: A single concentrated inpatient event drove most of the NV increase. TANF Standard acute hospital paid rose at INTERMOUNTAIN MEDICAL CENTER, and the matching IP Med/Surg heart-assist case carried very high paid per stay. This looks like a rare catastrophic case, not a broad-based hospital trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: One rare case can materially move spend, so leaders should avoid broad policy changes until the episode and payment terms are confirmed.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Validate the claim and case classification, then have clinical, UM, and network teams review level of care, transfer options, and reimbursement terms for this episode before taking broader action in NV.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in one provider and one apparent case with low-volume and low-baseline flags.
evidence_summary: NV TANF Standard acute hospital paid increased about $268K, entirely concentrated at INTERMOUNTAIN MEDICAL CENTER.
The related IP Med/Surg heart-assist case added about $268K on one new admission with very high paid per stay.
Both signals are low volume, indicating a one-case outlier rather than a sustained utilization shift.

business_patterns.top_pattern: KS ABD Non Dual inpatient musculoskeletal surgery costs rose on intensity
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: KS Medicaid ABD Non Dual acute hospital and IP Med/Surg
key_driver_codes: Other Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue O.R. Procedures with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: KS cost pressure is concentrated in one inpatient musculoskeletal surgery pattern within ABD Non Dual. Acute hospital paid increased alongside a matching IP Med/Surg diagnosis signal, while claim growth was limited. The business story is more about higher cost per stay or reimbursement intensity than broad admission growth.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is a focused inpatient cost issue that may be addressable through reimbursement review and targeted clinical criteria rather than broad utilization controls.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review pricing, coding, and medical-necessity support for this musculoskeletal inpatient pattern in KS, starting with reimbursement terms and any outlier payment behavior.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in a single DRG and diagnosis pattern, with limited claim growth and missing procedure detail.
evidence_summary: KS ABD Non Dual acute hospital paid increased about $260K in one musculoskeletal surgical DRG.
The matching IP Med/Surg diagnosis M952 added about $250K with no meaningful claim growth, pointing to higher intensity or reimbursement per stay.
Most of the increase is concentrated in a single inpatient service line.

business_patterns.top_pattern: MO and IN complication cases are surfacing in LTCH at high cost
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: MO and IN Medicaid LTCH and IP Med/Surg complication cases
business_patterns.pattern_details: Treatment-complication cases are creating concentrated cost in MO and IN, especially when they extend into LTCH care. MO shows both inpatient complication case growth and LTCH spend in the same complication DRG, with a smaller but similar LTCH signal in IN. This suggests episode escalation and costly post-acute placement, not a broad statewide utilization wave.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Complication cases that move into LTCH can drive longer, more expensive episodes and may signal avoidable variation in discharge planning or reimbursement.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review LTCH admission appropriateness, discharge planning, and reimbursement for Complications of Treatment with CC in MO and IN, starting with the larger MO cases.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The spend is concentrated in a small number of complication cases and LTCH claims with low-baseline flags.
evidence_summary: MO IP Med/Surg treatment-complication cases added about $146K, led by T8183XA at about $112K and T8131XA at about $35K.
MO TANF Standard LTCH paid added about $112K in Complications of Treatment with CC.
IN LTSS Non Dual LTCH added another about $25K in the same DRG.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Rare IP Med/Surg outliers are adding cost across FL / KS / NJ / TX
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: FL / KS / NJ / TX IP Med/Surg
key_driver_codes: Other Injury, Poisoning and Toxic Effect Diagnoses with MCC
Other Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue O.R. Procedures with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Several states show isolated high-cost inpatient Med/Surg cases rather than a single repeatable trend. The biggest contributors are injury/toxic-effect, musculoskeletal surgery, inflammatory bowel disease, and hernia-related admissions. These appear to be scattered rare cases that warrant case-level review, not broad clinical policy tightening.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Aggregated one-off cases can look like a trend, but the right response is targeted case management and validation rather than systemwide changes.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Have clinical and UM teams confirm these are isolated cases, validate coding where procedure detail is missing, and target case management only where repeat patterns emerge.
business_patterns.validation_reason: This pattern is built from low-baseline, single-case or few-case inpatient outliers across multiple states.
evidence_summary: Rare IP Med/Surg cases across FL / KS / NJ / TX added about $249K.
Largest contributors were Other Injury, Poisoning and Toxic Effect Diagnoses with MCC at about $81K and a musculoskeletal surgical outlier at about $59K.
Several diagnoses appear as one-case events with missing procedure detail.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Unmapped VERACYTE lab spending is a gating data and classification issue
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: NC / IA / KS / OH Medicaid lab and not-mapped facility reporting
business_patterns.pattern_details: Recurring unmapped classification is distorting the view of lab spend tied to VERACYTE across several states. NC shows a clinical lab pattern under Not Mapped DRG, and operational findings show additional VERACYTE spend in Not Mapped facility buckets across IA, KS, NC, and OH. This is a gating validation issue because provider mix, site-of-care, and authorization reporting may all be misclassified until mapping is fixed.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Leaders should not take provider or UM action on misclassified claims because the apparent trend may be partly a data issue.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Correct facility and clinical mapping for VERACYTE claims, then rerun provider, site-of-care, and authorization reporting before deciding on utilization or reimbursement actions.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Multiple groups carry unmapped or unknown flags, and the same provider appears across repeated Not Mapped buckets.
evidence_summary: NC OP Lab/Pthlgy spend tied to VERACYTE added about $38K, all tagged to Not Mapped DRG and pathology/lab.
Not Mapped facility claims for VERACYTE added about $27K across IA / KS / NC TANF Standard.
OH added another about $11K of unmapped VERACYTE spend across TANF Standard and ABD Non Dual.

business_patterns.top_pattern: TANF Standard acute hospital spend is rising through scattered one-off admissions
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: DC / FL / MO / VA / OH / CA Medicaid TANF Standard acute hospital
key_driver_codes: Other Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue O.R. Procedures with CC
Inguinal and Femoral Hernia Procedures without CC/MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: TANF Standard acute hospital cost growth across these states is coming from small clusters of isolated admissions, not a single recurring provider or diagnosis. Most cases show higher paid per stay, while CA is more volume-led with lower paid per stay. The aggregate effect is meaningful, but the pattern is too thin for broad policy or network action without case review.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Small one-off inpatient cases can add up, but the right response is targeted UM and payment validation rather than sweeping changes to TANF Standard.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Use UM to validate medical necessity and discharge planning for these cases, and escalate reimbursement review only where paid per stay is materially elevated.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is made up of low-baseline, highly concentrated admissions across several states.
evidence_summary: DC / FL / MO / VA TANF Standard acute hospital cases added about $64K, spread across several one-off inpatient DRGs.
OH contributed another about $59K in a single musculoskeletal surgical admission.
CA showed a smaller volume-led increase of about $7K, even with lower paid per stay.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Children's hospital admissions in TX and NJ are a small but concentrated cost pocket
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: TX and NJ Medicaid TANF Standard children's hospital inpatient
key_driver_codes: Other Injury, Poisoning and Toxic Effect Diagnoses with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: A few inpatient admissions at children's hospitals are driving a noticeable cost increase in TX and NJ. The cases are concentrated in injury/toxic-effect and inflammatory bowel disease admissions, with high paid per stay relative to the small number of claims. This points to pediatric site-of-care concentration rather than broad statewide utilization growth.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Children's hospitals can carry different reimbursement and referral dynamics, so targeted pediatric network and UM review is more appropriate than broad hospital action.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review pediatric referral patterns and children's hospital reimbursement for these diagnoses in TX and NJ before expanding broader inpatient controls.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase comes from only 5 admissions across two states and is highly concentrated by facility type.
evidence_summary: TX children's hospital paid added about $50K from 3 injury and toxic-effect admissions.
NJ children's hospital paid added about $50K from 2 inflammatory bowel disease admissions.
Both patterns are concentrated in a few high-cost stays.

business_patterns.top_pattern: TANF Foster Care acute hospital cases in NC and VA need targeted UM follow-up
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: NC / VA Medicaid TANF Foster Care acute hospital
key_driver_codes: Other Injury, Poisoning and Toxic Effect Diagnoses with MCC
Inguinal and Femoral Hernia Procedures without CC/MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: A small number of foster care acute hospital admissions are raising spend in NC and VA. Most of the increase is tied to injury and toxic-effect cases, with a smaller hernia-surgery signal in NC. Because volume is still low, this should be managed as targeted case review rather than product-wide tightening.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Even small inpatient spikes matter in foster care, where targeted UM and care management can reduce repeat high-cost events.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Route these admissions to UM and care management to confirm medical necessity, discharge support, and avoidable readmission risk for TANF Foster Care members.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The spend is concentrated in only a few admissions with low-baseline flags.
evidence_summary: NC / VA TANF Foster Care acute hospital paid increased about $51K.
Most of the increase came from Other Injury, Poisoning and Toxic Effect Diagnoses with MCC in NC and VA at about $41K combined.
A smaller hernia-surgery admission in NC added about $10K.

executive_summary.headline: The main story is a handful of concentrated inpatient outliers, plus one cross-state VERACYTE mapping issue that must be fixed before provider mix or UM actions are expanded.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: The largest cost increases are not broad utilization waves; they are concentrated in a few inpatient episodes in NV and KS, a treatment-complication and LTCH pattern in MO and IN, and smaller pediatric and foster care pockets. The most important gating issue is unmapped VERACYTE lab spend across several states, because it can misstate provider, site-of-care, and authorization views if left unresolved.
recommended_focus_order: Validate and correct unmapped VERACYTE claims before taking broader provider or UM action.
Address the concentrated NV and KS inpatient outliers through case-level clinical, UM, and reimbursement review.
Tighten LTCH, children's hospital, and other small-cluster inpatient follow-up where paid per stay is elevated.
